title: Cetera cum venero: lesser order left for an apostolic visit, not Mass dogma
source_text: XII. Igitur Bellarmini conjecturas & suspiciones nihil omnino moramur: Et tamen facile possumus ostendere, quod Bellarminus affirmat nos ostendere non posse, nempe, Paulum ibi nihil innuere de sacrificio Missae, & Sacramentorum materia & forma, aliisque gravioribus. Nam ipse loquendi modus, quo Apostolus utitur, satis indicat ipsum agere de rebus quae tanti momenti non sunt. Postquam enim institutionem Coenae Dominicae breviter exposuit, & reprehendit quosdam graviores abusus, qui apud Corinthios in celebratione illius obtinebant, subjungit verba illa, de quibus quaestio est, Cetera cum venero disponam. Ubi quivis qui textum attente considerabit, agnoscet facile Paulum innuere per caetera illa quaedam minoris momenti quam ea quae praecesserunt, & quae scribi nihil opus fuit, & quorum ordinatio in aliud tempus potuit sine periculo remitti, & videbatur requirere praesentiam Apostoli, qui praesens Ecclesiae Corinthiacae statum consideraret, & perpensis omnibus circumstantiis, statueret quid facto esset opus, & quae disciplina, quis ordo, in Ecclesia illa sequendus esset.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore we care nothing at all for Bellarmine's conjectures and suspicions: And yet we can easily show what Bellarmine affirms we cannot show, namely, that Paul there hints nothing concerning the sacrifice of the Mass, and the matter and form of the Sacraments, and other graver things. For the very manner of speaking which the Apostle uses sufficiently indicates that he is dealing with things which are not of such moment. For after he briefly set forth the institution of the Lord's Supper, and rebuked certain graver abuses which obtained among the Corinthians in its celebration, he subjoins those words about which the question is, The rest I will set in order when I come. Where anyone who will attentively consider the text will easily acknowledge that Paul hints by those remaining things certain things of lesser moment than those which preceded, and which there was no need to write, and whose arrangement could without danger be put off to another time, and seemed to require the presence of the Apostle, who being present would consider the state of the Corinthian Church, and all circumstances weighed, would decide what needed to be done, and what discipline, what order, should be followed in that Church.
pass_b_english: His conjectures weigh nothing — and the text itself undercuts them.
After fixing Supper institution and rebuking abuses, Paul adds: the rest when I come.
That rest is lesser business needing his presence and local judgment.
Not a coded deferral of Mass sacrifice and sacrament matter and form.
